market.question: Next US-Iran senior diplomatic meeting by September 30, 2026?
market.rules:
On September 22, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, with President Trump saying another meeting is scheduled in the near future.(see: https://www.israelhayom.com/2026/09/22/witkoff-kushner-attended-us-iran-meeting-another-expected-soon). 

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a direct or indirect senior-level diplomatic meeting between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting occurs when representatives of both listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in diplomacy on behalf of their respective governments or governing authorities deliberately meet for the purpose of diplomacy or negotiation. A qualifying meeting need not result in any agreement, joint statement, or further engagement.

A diplomatic meeting is senior-level if each listed entity is represented by a head of state, a head of government, or a vice president; a foreign minister; a minister of cabinet rank; the secretary or head of a national security council; the presiding officer of a national legislature; a special envoy; or another individual designated by the head of state or head of government to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. Individuals authorized only for technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, preparatory, or working-group-level talks will not be considered designated to conduct diplomatic negotiations on behalf of the head of state or head of government. This definition includes, but is not limited to, all of the following individuals: for the United States, Donald Trump, JD Vance, Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; and for Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei, Masoud Pezeshkian, Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. In each case, a qualifying representative must participate in the meeting.

A direct meeting refers to a diplomatic meeting where the representatives of both countries directly interact with each other in person. Meetings conducted through translators qualify, provided direct, face-to-face communication occurs. An indirect meeting refers to a meeting conducted indirectly through designated mediators or facilitators. A qualifying indirect meeting must meet both of the following criteria (i) the designated intermediaries act with the knowledge and authorization of both entities; (ii) representatives of both entities are physically present in the same facility, venue, or city as part of a single organized round of talks convened for the purpose of diplomatic engagement, with the intermediary conveying communications between the representatives or delegations on the same day. “The same day” means the same calendar day local time at the meeting location.

Sessions, proceedings, or convenings of standing international organizations, treaty bodies, or recurring multilateral summits or conferences (e.g., the United Nations General Assembly, G7, and G20 summits) do not qualify, unless a qualifying and deliberate diplomatic meeting between representatives of the listed countries is separately held alongside such a convening.

The following do not qualify as either a direct or indirect diplomatic meeting: chance encounters; standalone exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities; meetings conducted remotely, by telephone, or by any other means where the relevant representatives are not physically present at the same facility, venue, or city on the same day; discussions involving persons not authorized to engage in diplomacy or negotiation on behalf of their respective governments.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Trump renames AI by September 30?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs an executive order, proclamation, or presidential memorandum that adopts a new official name for artificial intelligence, or directs a federal agency or the federal government to adopt one, by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying action must replace or supersede "artificial intelligence" as the federal government's designation for the technology itself. Any replacement name qualifies, including "Superior Intelligence", "Extreme Intelligence", "Supreme Intelligence", or "Genius Intelligence"; the name chosen has no bearing on resolution. An order that directs an agency to adopt or implement such a name within a stated period qualifies.

Statements, speeches, interviews, press conferences, and social media posts, including polls posted to social media, do not count. Renaming a federal office, agency, program, task force, commission, or military service, such as an "AI Force", does not count unless the same action also renames the technology itself. Renaming a specific product, model, or private-sector system does not count. Incidental use of an alternative term in the text of an order, without a directive adopting it as the official designation, does not count.

The signing or issuance of a qualifying order within this market's timeframe will qualify for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of when the order takes effect, and regardless of whether it is subsequently stayed, enjoined, revoked, or superseded.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the government of the United States, including the text of presidential actions published at whitehouse.gov and in the Federal Register; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: No executive order, memorandum or other formal presidential document renaming AI had been signed. The article said: "As of yet, there is no official announcement from the White House on how this is to be implemented."
The article reported that there had been no executive order about 'super intelligence' yet, and that it was unclear what, if anything, would follow from the announcement.

In his September 22 speech to the UN General Assembly, Trump said that 'from this point forward, all of United States documents' would use 'super intelligence' instead of 'artificial intelligence'. The announcement was made in a speech, not a signed order.

The State Department's international organisations bureau told staff to switch terms in an email from Deputy Assistant Secretary Michael Drager titled 'Change in Nomenclature AI to SI'. The email said: 'Following the president's remarks at the GA today, please change all references of Artificial Intelligence to Super Intelligence.' It was an agency email, not a presidential order.

On September 19, Trump posted a poll on X and Truth Social asking which name should replace 'Artificial Intelligence': Superior, Extreme or Supreme Intelligence. 'Superior Intelligence' had about 39% on X, and the poll drew more than 140,000 votes within a day.
On September 21, Trump posted on Truth Social that he would 'only encourage AI or, SI (SUPER INTELLIGENCE)!', the day before his UN speech.
Trump said he had pitched the 'super intelligence' rebrand to Chinese President Xi Jinping and claimed Xi liked the idea.

Earlier Trump renamings were done by executive order: the Gulf of Mexico became the 'Gulf of America' by executive order in 2025. In August 2026 Lake Ontario was renamed 'Lake America' during a trade dispute with Canada.

The 'Department of War' secondary title for the Defense Department was also made formal by an executive order, signed on September 5, 2025, after officials said it was coming. The Gulf of America order was signed on January 20, 2025, about two weeks after Trump first floated the name on January 7.

The window closes on September 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET, about 2–3 days from today. Only a signed executive order, proclamation or presidential memorandum counts; speeches, social media posts and agency emails do not. The primary resolution source is whitehouse.gov and the Federal Register.

market.question: Will Benjamin Netanyahu be the next Prime Minister of Israel?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: September polls disagree widely. Channel 14 has Likud 32, Yashar 22 and the right-wing bloc at 63. i24NEWS has Likud 27, Yashar 22 and the coalition at 60. Maariv has Yashar 22, Likud 18, coalition 49 and Zionist opposition 55. N12 has Yashar 23, Likud 20, coalition 50 and opposition 66 (54 Zionist + 12 Arab). Channel 13 has Yashar 22, Likud 18, opposition 52 and coalition 51.
Averaged across the polls, Likud has 23 seats, Eisenkot's Yashar 22.2, Bennett–Lapid's B'Yachad 10.6 and the Arab parties 12.4. Likud's figure ranges from 18 to 32 seats depending on the pollster.

The Channel 13 poll gave Eisenkot's bloc 52 seats and Netanyahu's bloc 51. Neither reaches the 61 needed to govern. Hendel's Reservists party crossed the threshold with 4 seats for the first time in Channel 13 polling.

In an average of mainstream polls, Netanyahu's bloc (including Winter) is at 53.6 seats and the Zionist opposition bloc at 53.4. The non-Arab opposition cannot reach a majority without the Arab parties, which win about 12 seats.

On September 26, 2026, the opposition leaders signed a declaration of principles to cooperate in the run-up to the October 27 election. The signers were Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar), Avigdor Liberman (Yisrael Beiteinu), Yair Golan (The Democrats), and Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid (Together).

President Herzog said that if neither bloc reaches 61 seats he will 'do everything so that there will not be repeat elections,' and he raised unity or rotation governments as options. He also suggested the Netanyahu pardon question could come into compromise talks. Netanyahu's trial is ongoing, and he has reportedly not answered Herzog's proposal to mediate a plea deal.

Haredi parties are reportedly preparing a possible shift in strategy after the election. They may not recommend any prime minister candidate at first and may stay outside the new coalition until the draft-law crisis is resolved.

Eisenkot says the Jewish opposition parties (Yashar, Beyahad, Yisrael Beiteinu, Democrats) will win 61 or more seats without Arab parties. No mainstream poll has shown either bloc at 61. Bennett–Lapid and Liberman have ruled out Arab parties in a future coalition, and Netanyahu's campaign attacks Eisenkot over possible reliance on Arab parties.

The Knesset dissolved on July 17, 2026, and election day is October 27, 2026. Diplomatic voting is on October 20, and official results are confirmed on November 4, 2026. Candidate lists were due September 8, and the electoral threshold is 3.25%.

The question resolves only when a prime minister is formally sworn in after the 2026 election. A caretaker prime minister, including Netanyahu staying on as interim PM, does not count. The questions close on October 27, 2026, which is election day and comes before any government can be sworn in.

Recent gaps from election to swearing-in: 404 days from April 2019 to May 14, 2020, spanning three elections; about 81 days after March 23, 2021 (Bennett–Lapid government sworn in June 13, 2021); about 58 days after November 1, 2022 (Netanyahu sworn in December 29, 2022).

Of the five elections from April 2019 to November 2022, 3 led to a sworn-in government (2020 Netanyahu–Gantz rotation, 2021 Bennett–Lapid, 2022 Netanyahu). The April 2019 and September 2019 elections produced no government. Netanyahu became PM after 2 of those 3 formations.

market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 15?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: The National reported that the East-West pipeline had restarted and was pumping at a low rate. Its only sources were unnamed Reuters sources and satellite-data analysis. The article cited no statement from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy, the government or Aramco.

The Reuters story, headlined 'Saudi Arabia restarts East-West oil pipeline, to resume exports from Yanbu, sources say', credits the restart to unnamed sources. Aramco was trying to bring flow back to 4 million bpd, below the system's full capacity of 7 million bpd.

The Saudi-owned Asharq Al-Awsat also carried the restart under the headline 'Sources: Saudi Arabia Restarts East-West Oil Pipeline', so the report is again attributed to sources and not to an official announcement.
Sources said reaching about 40% of capacity would take a couple of days and a full restart would take 6 to 8 weeks. Another source put the full restart at up to six weeks.

Pumping has resumed at reduced rates, and tanker loadings at Yanbu appear to have restarted this week, but regular exports have not recovered. Two tankers due to load on September 23 had not loaded, and six more were scheduled for September 24–27.

Sources said volumes on the East-West pipeline were building but tanker loading at Yanbu was delayed. Reuters reported that Aramco told European refiners it first needed to build a 'critical mass' of crude at Yanbu.
Industrial Info Resources cited satellite imagery showing vessels loading crude at Yanbu after the pipeline attack.

The Ministry of Energy's statement on SPA was headlined 'East–West Pipeline Shut Down as a Precaution Following Multiple Attacks'. The ministry also posted it on X and said emergency teams were deployed to secure the pipeline and assess its safety.

Saudi Arabia shut the East-West crude pipeline after several drone attacks launched from Iraq hit it in the Riyadh and Medina regions. Satellite imagery and industry sources reported that 3 of its 11 pumping stations were damaged.

There is a precedent from April 2026. On April 9 the Ministry of Energy said attacks had cut about 700,000 bpd of East-West pipeline capacity, and around April 12 it announced on SPA that full pumping capacity of about 7 million bpd had been restored.

Argaam carried the April Ministry of Energy statement that the energy facilities and the East-West line had recovered and regained their operating capacity. The ministry has made such a restoration announcement at least once before.

The 1,200 km pipeline links the eastern oil fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu and has been rerouting about 4 million bpd around the Strait of Hormuz. The Saudi Foreign Ministry said Riyadh would hold off retaliating to give Iraq's government time to stop attacks from its territory.
The US Energy Secretary said the Saudi East-West pipeline would be back in operation within days. This came from a third party (not the Saudi government) and was about the future.

The questions resolve Yes only if official Saudi government information says the pipeline is operating now; partial capacity counts. Reports from anonymous sources or third parties, satellite data, and forward-looking statements do not count. Searches through 2026-09-27 found no Saudi official statement confirming the September restart.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $100 in September?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of September 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Next US-Iran senior diplomatic meeting by September 30, 2026?
market.rules:
On September 22, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, with President Trump saying another meeting is scheduled in the near future.(see: https://www.israelhayom.com/2026/09/22/witkoff-kushner-attended-us-iran-meeting-another-expected-soon). 

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a direct or indirect senior-level diplomatic meeting between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting occurs when representatives of both listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in diplomacy on behalf of their respective governments or governing authorities deliberately meet for the purpose of diplomacy or negotiation. A qualifying meeting need not result in any agreement, joint statement, or further engagement.

A diplomatic meeting is senior-level if each listed entity is represented by a head of state, a head of government, or a vice president; a foreign minister; a minister of cabinet rank; the secretary or head of a national security council; the presiding officer of a national legislature; a special envoy; or another individual designated by the head of state or head of government to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. Individuals authorized only for technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, preparatory, or working-group-level talks will not be considered designated to conduct diplomatic negotiations on behalf of the head of state or head of government. This definition includes, but is not limited to, all of the following individuals: for the United States, Donald Trump, JD Vance, Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; and for Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei, Masoud Pezeshkian, Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. In each case, a qualifying representative must participate in the meeting.

A direct meeting refers to a diplomatic meeting where the representatives of both countries directly interact with each other in person. Meetings conducted through translators qualify, provided direct, face-to-face communication occurs. An indirect meeting refers to a meeting conducted indirectly through designated mediators or facilitators. A qualifying indirect meeting must meet both of the following criteria (i) the designated intermediaries act with the knowledge and authorization of both entities; (ii) representatives of both entities are physically present in the same facility, venue, or city as part of a single organized round of talks convened for the purpose of diplomatic engagement, with the intermediary conveying communications between the representatives or delegations on the same day. “The same day” means the same calendar day local time at the meeting location.

Sessions, proceedings, or convenings of standing international organizations, treaty bodies, or recurring multilateral summits or conferences (e.g., the United Nations General Assembly, G7, and G20 summits) do not qualify, unless a qualifying and deliberate diplomatic meeting between representatives of the listed countries is separately held alongside such a convening.

The following do not qualify as either a direct or indirect diplomatic meeting: chance encounters; standalone exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities; meetings conducted remotely, by telephone, or by any other means where the relevant representatives are not physically present at the same facility, venue, or city on the same day; discussions involving persons not authorized to engage in diplomacy or negotiation on behalf of their respective governments.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Trump renames AI by September 30?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs an executive order, proclamation, or presidential memorandum that adopts a new official name for artificial intelligence, or directs a federal agency or the federal government to adopt one, by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying action must replace or supersede "artificial intelligence" as the federal government's designation for the technology itself. Any replacement name qualifies, including "Superior Intelligence", "Extreme Intelligence", "Supreme Intelligence", or "Genius Intelligence"; the name chosen has no bearing on resolution. An order that directs an agency to adopt or implement such a name within a stated period qualifies.

Statements, speeches, interviews, press conferences, and social media posts, including polls posted to social media, do not count. Renaming a federal office, agency, program, task force, commission, or military service, such as an "AI Force", does not count unless the same action also renames the technology itself. Renaming a specific product, model, or private-sector system does not count. Incidental use of an alternative term in the text of an order, without a directive adopting it as the official designation, does not count.

The signing or issuance of a qualifying order within this market's timeframe will qualify for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of when the order takes effect, and regardless of whether it is subsequently stayed, enjoined, revoked, or superseded.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the government of the United States, including the text of presidential actions published at whitehouse.gov and in the Federal Register; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: No executive order, memorandum or other formal presidential document renaming AI had been signed. The article said: "As of yet, there is no official announcement from the White House on how this is to be implemented."
The article reported that there had been no executive order about 'super intelligence' yet, and that it was unclear what, if anything, would follow from the announcement.

In his September 22 speech to the UN General Assembly, Trump said that 'from this point forward, all of United States documents' would use 'super intelligence' instead of 'artificial intelligence'. The announcement was made in a speech, not a signed order.

The State Department's international organisations bureau told staff to switch terms in an email from Deputy Assistant Secretary Michael Drager titled 'Change in Nomenclature AI to SI'. The email said: 'Following the president's remarks at the GA today, please change all references of Artificial Intelligence to Super Intelligence.' It was an agency email, not a presidential order.

On September 19, Trump posted a poll on X and Truth Social asking which name should replace 'Artificial Intelligence': Superior, Extreme or Supreme Intelligence. 'Superior Intelligence' had about 39% on X, and the poll drew more than 140,000 votes within a day.
On September 21, Trump posted on Truth Social that he would 'only encourage AI or, SI (SUPER INTELLIGENCE)!', the day before his UN speech.
Trump said he had pitched the 'super intelligence' rebrand to Chinese President Xi Jinping and claimed Xi liked the idea.

Earlier Trump renamings were done by executive order: the Gulf of Mexico became the 'Gulf of America' by executive order in 2025. In August 2026 Lake Ontario was renamed 'Lake America' during a trade dispute with Canada.

The 'Department of War' secondary title for the Defense Department was also made formal by an executive order, signed on September 5, 2025, after officials said it was coming. The Gulf of America order was signed on January 20, 2025, about two weeks after Trump first floated the name on January 7.

The window closes on September 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET, about 2–3 days from today. Only a signed executive order, proclamation or presidential memorandum counts; speeches, social media posts and agency emails do not. The primary resolution source is whitehouse.gov and the Federal Register.

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Of the five elections from April 2019 to November 2022, 3 led to a sworn-in government (2020 Netanyahu–Gantz rotation, 2021 Bennett–Lapid, 2022 Netanyahu). The April 2019 and September 2019 elections produced no government. Netanyahu became PM after 2 of those 3 formations.

market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

recent_facts.fact: The National reported that the East-West pipeline had restarted and was pumping at a low rate. Its only sources were unnamed Reuters sources and satellite-data analysis. The article cited no statement from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy, the government or Aramco.

The Reuters story, headlined 'Saudi Arabia restarts East-West oil pipeline, to resume exports from Yanbu, sources say', credits the restart to unnamed sources. Aramco was trying to bring flow back to 4 million bpd, below the system's full capacity of 7 million bpd.

The Saudi-owned Asharq Al-Awsat also carried the restart under the headline 'Sources: Saudi Arabia Restarts East-West Oil Pipeline', so the report is again attributed to sources and not to an official announcement.
Sources said reaching about 40% of capacity would take a couple of days and a full restart would take 6 to 8 weeks. Another source put the full restart at up to six weeks.

Pumping has resumed at reduced rates, and tanker loadings at Yanbu appear to have restarted this week, but regular exports have not recovered. Two tankers due to load on September 23 had not loaded, and six more were scheduled for September 24–27.

Sources said volumes on the East-West pipeline were building but tanker loading at Yanbu was delayed. Reuters reported that Aramco told European refiners it first needed to build a 'critical mass' of crude at Yanbu.
Industrial Info Resources cited satellite imagery showing vessels loading crude at Yanbu after the pipeline attack.

The Ministry of Energy's statement on SPA was headlined 'East–West Pipeline Shut Down as a Precaution Following Multiple Attacks'. The ministry also posted it on X and said emergency teams were deployed to secure the pipeline and assess its safety.

Saudi Arabia shut the East-West crude pipeline after several drone attacks launched from Iraq hit it in the Riyadh and Medina regions. Satellite imagery and industry sources reported that 3 of its 11 pumping stations were damaged.

There is a precedent from April 2026. On April 9 the Ministry of Energy said attacks had cut about 700,000 bpd of East-West pipeline capacity, and around April 12 it announced on SPA that full pumping capacity of about 7 million bpd had been restored.

Argaam carried the April Ministry of Energy statement that the energy facilities and the East-West line had recovered and regained their operating capacity. The ministry has made such a restoration announcement at least once before.

The 1,200 km pipeline links the eastern oil fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu and has been rerouting about 4 million bpd around the Strait of Hormuz. The Saudi Foreign Ministry said Riyadh would hold off retaliating to give Iraq's government time to stop attacks from its territory.
The US Energy Secretary said the Saudi East-West pipeline would be back in operation within days. This came from a third party (not the Saudi government) and was about the future.

The questions resolve Yes only if official Saudi government information says the pipeline is operating now; partial capacity counts. Reports from anonymous sources or third parties, satellite data, and forward-looking statements do not count. Searches through 2026-09-27 found no Saudi official statement confirming the September restart.
